text:
maria_sales: Heads-up: Acme POC failing — several 401s and a token-boundary 403. Demo scheduled for tomorrow, can we swarm?

jordan_se: Which endpoint and any logs?

maria_sales: They hit /v1/generate. Example curl they ran:
```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx' -H 'x-org-id:acme-inc' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}'```
They see 401 sometimes, 403 other times. Body sometimes says 'tenant_binding_mismatch'.

owen_support: Can you paste a raw response body? 403s generally are "project_mismatch" or "insufficient_scope".

maria_sales: Pasted from their logs:
```json
{"error":"Forbidden","reason":"tenant_binding_mismatch","details":"key bound to org 'acme' but request x-org 'acme-inc'","request_id":"rz-9a8b7c"}
```

tina_ps: Acme told us their org slug is 'acme' in the console, but their infra uses 'acme-inc' in headers for historical reasons. They also said they rotate keys between demo/prod projects.

harry_eng: Likely root causes:
1) Exact-match tenant binding: token claim for org == 'acme' vs header 'acme-inc' -> mismatch.
2) Newer keys require explicit scope 'inference:generate' for sk keys minted after 2025-03-01; if rotated key is missing scope -> 401/403.

jordan_se: Quick repro steps we can ask them to try?

harry_eng: Ask them to: 1) decode JWT to inspect claims, 2) try removing x-org header to let token-driven routing, 3) verify the key's scopes in console.
Example to decode payload: 
```bash
echo 'eyJhbGciOi...' | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 --decode | jq
```
Look for "org" and "scopes" claims.

owen_support: Workarounds: 1) Create a temporary demo-scoped key bound to 'acme-inc' and share, or 2) update their x-org header to match key binding. I can provision a temp key if PS approves.

maria_sales: Acme asked if changing header or rotating key affects pricing / entitlements — they were worried about enterprise rate limits for the demo.

tina_ps: No pricing impact for a short POC key. If they need sustained higher throughput we can increase their rate limit for the trial. I can open an internal request to bump quota for 48h.

harry_eng: Also noticed a recent deploy touching tenant binding validation (canaryed yesterday). Log snippet:
```
request_id=rz-9a8b7c component=tenant-bind-check level=warn msg="binding check failed" expected_org=acme received_header=acme-inc
```
We should decide whether to accept common suffix variants; doing so has security implications. I'll push a small normalization PR to allow a configurable alias map.

deploy-bot: deploybot: canary-policy applied to tenant-binding-validator v2 at 2025-03-10T13:12:00Z

harry_eng: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/tenant-bindings/pull/789 — adds alias map and a fallback debug-log to surface mismatches. Planning to roll to staging and monitor.

owen_support: I'll create support ticket #4567 with attachments (logs, sample curl) and assign to eng-infra. Also issuing a temporary demo key bound to 'acme-inc' (expires in 24h) and emailing it to the Acme POC contact.

maria_sales: Thanks. Can you also include instructions to check the key in console (https://console.redwood.ai/keys): view "Binding" and "Scopes" fields, rotate if missing scopes.

tina_ps: Adding note for security questionnaire: confirm that demo key is short-lived and limited to inference:generate scope. I'll record this in the questionnaire response.

maria_sales: Great — I'm going to send the temporary key and ask them to test. Please ping here when PR merges or ticket updated. :thumbsup:

harry_eng: Will monitor logs for request_id rz-9a8b7c and related errors. If alias map looks safe in staging, we can ship it to production after sign-off.

maria_sales: Closing loop once Acme confirms demo passes. Thanks everyone.
